A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from EFFI-CODE to SWIFTCODER, with substantial methodological revisions. All 16 pages of v1 and 13 pages of v3 are readable. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; v1's reference to 'Appendix ??' is unresolved.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset-construction statistics, fine-tuning results, ablations, baseline comparisons, and repeated execution measurements in Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–9.

after.justification: v3 reports original training-data efficiency correlations, dataset statistics, and fine-tuning evaluations across several benchmarks and programming languages in Figures 3–4 and Tables 1–7.

M1.justification: v1 constructs training solutions through five SOAP optimization cycles using a DeepSeek teacher and line-level overhead feedback. v3's abstract, Section 3.2, and Figure 1 instead describe generating candidates with multiple LLMs and selecting solutions through execution-time and memory measurements. This substantially replaces the central construction procedure, although a residual SOAP reference remains.

E1.justification: Training expands from eight sources of Python tasks to nine sources, adding SelfCodeAlign and C++, Java, Rust, and Go. Evaluation adds MBPPPlus, DS-1000 data-science tasks, EvoEval Tool_Use/Subtle/Creative scenarios, and HumanEval-X C++/Java tasks. EffiBench and the HumanEval task family remain represented.

E2.justification: v3 adds an evaluated Mercury baseline alongside PIE in Table 7; Mercury was only cited in v1. Conversely, v1's comparisons against canonical-solution fine-tuning and alternative GPT-4o/Claude teacher-generated datasets disappear from the reported comparisons. These changes affect both external baselines and alternative training-data methods.

E3.justification: The reported training corpus grows from 9,451 to 65,710 tasks, while the four-epoch SFT schedule and principal hyperparameters remain unchanged. HumanEval evaluation switches to HumanEvalPlus. Model-scale testing changes from DeepSeek 1.3B–33B on HumanEval to Qwen 1.5B–14B on EffiBench, and v3 introduces a varying-training-efficiency experimental design.

E4.justification: The canonical-versus-optimized training comparison becomes a multi-level efficiency-correlation study in v3 Section 3.1 and Figure 3. v1's dataset-fraction, teacher-choice, DPO/ORPO, and execution-stability analyses are removed. Model-size testing continues with different models and placement, rather than disappearing entirely.

E5.justification: v1 Table 8 reports five executions of one fine-tuned model, including means and standard deviations; v3 removes this limited variability assessment. v3 adds correlation coefficients and fitted lines in Figure 3 without confidence intervals or repeated-run information. The main performance tables remain point estimates.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and extended. For Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct on EffiBench, baseline/fine-tuned pass@1 changes from 3.3%/61.0% in v1 Table 2 to 44.8%/57.7% in v3 Table 2. Changed training data, construction procedures, and correct-task overlaps prevent treating these as controlled cross-version gains. New benchmark and Mercury results accompany removal of earlier ablation results.

T1.justification: v1 explicitly defines a preference dataset consisting of prompts, preferred efficient completions, and dispreferred original completions for DPO/ORPO. v3 removes this mathematical definition with that experimental branch. Neither version contains theorems, proofs, or substantial theoretical derivations.

C1.justification: The central claim of improving both correctness and efficiency remains. However, v1's contribution centers on an open-source teacher's iterative self-optimization, whereas v3 explicitly claims a versatile, multilingual dataset-construction framework using multiple generators. This substantially broadens and redefines the claimed contribution beyond renaming.

C2.justification: The interpretation that efficient training code improves generated-code efficiency remains. v3 adds qualifications that runtime benefits are more widespread than peak-memory benefits and DS-1000 efficiency gains are modest, plus discussion of language-specific source biases. Earlier interpretations concerning training-data quantity and open-source teacher adequacy are removed.

D1.justification: v1 documents GPT-3.5-turbo test-generation/filtering steps, profiling libraries, a specific teacher checkpoint, and the inference-prompt choice. v3 replaces much of this detail with a shorter construction description and a SelfCodeAlign filtering citation. It also drops the direct project-code URL, while retaining open-source intentions and the main SFT hyperparameters.

R1.justification: The related-work sections remain largely intact. v3 adds references for SelfCodeAlign, EvalPlus, DS-1000, EvoEval, and HumanEval-X, while removing DPO, ORPO, and DeepSeek-Coder-V2 references. It newly distinguishes its candidate-selection approach from SOAP and Mercury, both already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, abstract, and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten. The detailed construction sections become a preliminary study followed by compressed construction and statistics sections. Experiments are reorganized into Python, data-science, multilingual, and baseline comparisons, and a broader-impacts section is added.

P2.justification: The document switches from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 is redrawn, its existing code examples become a separate Figure 2, and correlation plots are added. The distribution figure has revised axes and scope. Table 1 changes from filtering-stage counts to source-by-language counts, and experimental tables are substantially reorganized.

improvement.justification: v3's data-science, evolved-task, and C++/Java evaluations and Mercury comparison strengthen evidence of generality and competitiveness. However, it removes v1's controlled ablations, execution-variability assessment, and substantial construction detail. Its revised selection pipeline also conflicts with residual SOAP wording, while Section 3.3 retains numerical summaries inconsistent with Figure 4. Broader validation and weaker reproducibility/internal consistency coexist, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
